name: Côtes du Rhône Villages

limits: For red and rosé wine, Grenache: at least 40%
For red and rosé wine, Mourvèdre and Syrah together: at least 25%

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.

notes: Grenache-based Côtes du Rhône Villages typically has a chewy fruitiness.

blurb.text: A Rhône Valley appellation listed under the Southern Rhône, usable in a limited part of the region. Its label may add one of 21 named places, such as Séguret, Sablet or Plan de Dieu.
